findings.title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
findings.body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper passes an optional caller callback rather than refetching that query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. Consequently, deleting the cache can show a success toast while continuing to display the old cache timestamp and deletion action until the page is reloaded. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve cache status for in-memory delegation credentials
findings.body: Connected calendars can use in-memory delegation credentials, but this lookup assumes every displayed credential ID is a database credential ID. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles in-memory credentials by querying userId and the cache key, since their cache is stored under a real credential ID. Looking up status solely using the displayed credential ID therefore returns no status for those delegated calendars even when availability is being served from cache. Since the dropdown hides all cache actions when cacheUpdatedAt is null, affected users cannot inspect or clear that cache. Resolve the user's backing cache records for delegated connections and support that same identity in the deletion flow.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script's directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore edits or creates an .env outside the repository, leaving the application's GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged despite printing success. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before locating .env.

findings.title: Use an environment-file replacement compatible with GNU sed
findings.body: The sed -i '' syntax requires BSD sed. On Linux with GNU sed, the empty argument is interpreted as the editing script and this command fails instead of replacing an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Because the failure is unchecked, the script still reports that the URL was updated, leaving webhook testing pointed at the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement approach or handle the sed variants explicitly and check the result.
